## Two GPS Decisions on Selective Availability

Selective Availability deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. The US government addressed the feature in two distinct steps: it stopped using it in May 2000, then announced in September 2007 that the future GPS III generation would be procured without it.

At President Bill Clinton’s direction, the government stopped using Selective Availability in May 2000 to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide. The September 2007 announcement addressed a different question—not whether to keep using the feature, but whether it would be included in a future generation. The GPS III generation would be procured without it, making the 2000 policy durable.
